raw_response:
I've farmed these 20 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Me and the old lady, we're the only ones home now — our son works in Shijiazhuang. I never went to school, but I know my land. I don't trust those book numbers much; I trust what I've seen with my own eyes and what the neighbors do.

I keep 12 mu for wheat then maize, and 8 mu for cotton. That's what I've always done, though some years I think about giving up the cotton because it's hard on our backs. But cotton money is decent when the price holds, and that plot in the south has grown cotton since before I was born.

**Wheat** — I sowed it last October around the 10th, before the cold came. Now it's March and the wheat is waking up. I always put down base fertilizer in the fall — about half a bag of compound per mu and some phosphorus. This spring, when it turns green, I'll topdress with urea, maybe a quarter bag per mu. I know people talk about kilograms, but I think in bags. A bag of urea is 40 jin, so that's about 10 jin per mu for the topdress, maybe 20 jin total for the year counting the fall. My neighbor cut back last year and his wheat was thin. I'm not taking that risk. I'll water it three times total — green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Pumping costs money, so I watch the sky, but wheat can't go thirsty. I hire the combine for harvest in early June; me and the old lady can't swing a scythe anymore. I expect around 400–450 jin per mu if the weather behaves.

**Maize** — Right after the wheat comes off in mid-June, I got to get the maize in fast. The window is barely a week. I hire the machine to plant — I don't have my own planter. I buy hybrid seed, about 3 jin per mu. At planting I put compound fertilizer in the row, about half a bag per mu. If the leaves look yellow at jointing, I'll throw on some urea, but usually the base dose is enough. Two irrigations: one when it's knee-high, one at tasseling. Summer rains help, so I don't water as much as wheat. Harvest is late September. Should get 500 jin per mu, maybe a bit less if it's dry.

**Cotton** — I plant the 8 mu around April 20th, after the last cold snap. Cotton needs warmth. I plough and harrow that field good — it gets hard over winter. I put compound fertilizer down before planting, not too much, maybe 20 jin per mu of compound, and a little urea when it flowers. I irrigate twice, once after planting to help it sprout, and once in July when the bolls are setting. Cotton needs spraying — bollworms come every year without fail. I spray insecticide three times and herbicide once. The hard part is picking. September through October, me and the old lady are out there every day bending down. If the bolls open heavy, I might hire two women from the east village for a few days. I hope for about 200 jin of lint per mu, but some years it's only 150 jin.

I'm careful with cash. Fertilizer and seed prices keep climbing. I spend around 6,000 yuan on all the inputs for the year. I don't borrow if I can help it. When I'm unsure, I do what I did last year. Last year was decent, not great. That's good enough for me.
